headline: Maintain a compact prefix of nonzero values
statement: Move all zero values to the end of nums in place while preserving the order of nonzero values. The method returns nothing.
intuition: Maintain a compact prefix of nonzero values. Each encountered nonzero moves to the next free prefix position; swapping leaves zeros behind.
approach: Set write=0 and scan read left to right.
For each nonzero, swap nums[read] with nums[write] and advance write.
Ignore zeros; after the scan they occupy the remaining suffix.
correctness: Before each scan step, nums[:write] contains precisely the encountered nonzero values in original order. Swapping the next nonzero into write appends it to that prefix; positions skipped between write and read contain zeros. At termination every nonzero is in the prefix and all remaining values are zero.
bruteForce: Repeatedly remove a zero and append it to the end, shifting many array elements: O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); auxiliary space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Mutate nums rather than returning a newly allocated array.
Advancing write for zeros leaves holes in the compact prefix.
